ci_method: Wild cluster bootstrap (Rademacher weights, 4999 reps, imposing the null, clustered on the 60 practices) around the visit-level 2x2 DiD OLS; 95% interval. Agrees with CR1 cluster-robust SEs using t(59) critical values [6.09, 10.03], with clustering on member [5.93, 10.19], with the practice-period collapsed WLS DiD [5.40, 10.73], and with a practice-level Welch t-test on the 60 pre-to-post changes [6.01, 9.99]. Randomization inference (5000 permutations of the program label across the 60 practices) gives p < 0.0002.
specifications_run: PRIMARY: visit-level 2x2 DiD OLS, outcome = any PCP visit on ED date through ED date +14; PCP visit = office E&M 99204/99212-99215 at POS 11 billed by Family Medicine or Internal Medicine, OR hospital-outpatient primary care clinic visit G0463 at POS 22 with revenue code 0517/0519; ED visit = member-date with a POS 23 claim carrying an ED E&M 99281-99285; cluster-robust SE by practice. Estimate +8.06 pp

Same spec but PCP visit = office E&M at POS 11 by FM/IM only (drops hospital-based primary care clinic visits). Estimate +2.46 pp. DISCARDED as the primary measure: it omits ~23% of every practice's primary care visit volume and ~3/4 of the program's effect
Same spec but PCP visit = G0463 revenue 0517/0519 channel only. Estimate +6.31 pp
PCP visit = office E&M + G0463 revenue 0517 only (excluding revenue 0519 'other clinic'). Estimate +7.91 pp

PCP visit = any office E&M 99204/99212-99215 at POS 11 regardless of rendering specialty (i.e. counting specialist office visits as PCP follow-up). Estimate +2.12 pp. DISCARDED: counts Cardiology/GI/Derm/Endo/Ortho office visits as primary care
PCP visit = any-specialty POS 11 office E&M + G0463. Estimate +7.55 pp. DISCARDED for the same reason
TWFE: practice fixed effects + calendar-month fixed effects + program x post, primary outcome. Estimate +8.03 pp
Primary outcome + ED acuity (99281-99285) controls. Estimate +8.06 pp
Primary outcome, 7-day follow-up window. Estimate +2.42 pp
Primary outcome, 30-day follow-up window. Estimate +6.50 pp (flagged: right-censored for ED visits after 15 Dec 2025, since the extract ends 14 Jan 2026, so not directly comparable)
Primary outcome, days 1-14 only (same-day follow-up excluded). Estimate +7.71 pp
Practice x period collapsed WLS DiD (60 practices x 2 periods, weighted by ED visits). Estimate +8.06 pp
Practice-level Welch t-test on the 60 practice-specific pre-to-post changes in follow-up rate. Estimate +8.00 pp, p = 5.5e-11

Monthly event study, program x calendar-month interactions with practice FE, June 2025 as reference. Jul-Dec coefficients +12.7, +11.7, +7.3, +8.3, +8.6, +9.7 pp; all pre-period coefficients jointly insignificant (F = 1.36, p = 0.26)
DiD with group-specific linear time trend over the full year. Estimate +8.96 pp
DiD with calendar-month FE plus group-specific linear trend. Estimate +7.21 pp

Pre-trend-extrapolated DiD: pre-period (Jan-Jun) differential linear trend projected into the post period and subtracted. Estimate +2.29 pp, practice cluster-bootstrap CI [-2.74, +7.01]. Reported as a sensitivity rather than the headline, because the pre-period drift sits entirely in the office channel and in the control arm's month-to-month noise, not in the channel carrying the effect (see assumptions). Same adjustment applied channel-by-channel: clinic channel +5.65 pp (effect survives), office channel -1.40 pp (effect does not)
June-2025-only baseline DiD (drops the noisy early pre-period months). Estimate +6.05 pp [+2.73, +9.37]; by channel, clinic +6.66 pp, office +1.30 pp

Placebo DiD inside the pre-period only, fake launch 1 Apr 2025. Primary outcome +2.93 pp (p = 0.029), office-only outcome +1.84 pp (p = 0.17) - a warning sign that pre-period monthly rates are noisy, discussed under assumptions
Logit with the same four terms; implied DiD in probabilities +8.06 pp
Within-member DiD (member FE, 1,828 members with ED visits in both periods). Estimate +4.53 pp, se 3.99, p = 0.26 - same sign, badly underpowered
Randomization inference permuting the program label across the 60 practices (5,000 draws): primary outcome p < 0.0002, clinic channel p < 0.0002, office channel p = 0.016
assumptions_checked: ED visit definition / double counting: every POS 23 claim pairs a facility claim (revenue 0450) with a professional claim (Emergency Medicine), so an encounter generates 2-9 claim IDs and 2.55 claim IDs on average. Counting claim IDs would have given 79,691 'ED visits'; collapsing to member-service-date gives 31,260. All 31,260 POS 23 member-dates carry an ED E&M 99281-99285, and no 99281-99285 or revenue 045x line appears outside POS 23, so the POS-based and code-based definitions agree exactly. 22 member-dates carry two ED E&M levels (duplicate or genuinely repeat same-day encounters); counted once each

PCP visit definition - the decision that drives the answer: 76,877 visits (23% of all primary care visits, present at every one of the 60 practices) are billed as G0463 at POS 22 with revenue code 0517 ('clinic - family practice clinic', 84%) or 0519 ('clinic - other', 16%), i.e. provider-based/hospital-outpatient primary care, with no professional-claim counterpart anywhere in the extract. Checked that these are genuine, standalone primary care encounters and not facility add-ons to office visits: only 0.57% share a date with a POS 11 PCP office E&M; 97% have a same-day venipuncture (36415, revenue 0300) at POS 22; mean allowed $115 vs $98 for an office E&M; 56,621 of 119,560 members have at least one, and member-level G0463 counts correlate -0.09 with office-visit counts (partial site substitution). Excluding them understates the 2025 follow-up rate (27.6% vs 35.2%) and misses roughly three quarters of the program effect (+2.46 pp vs +8.06 pp)

Specialist contamination: POS 11 office E&M codes are also billed by Cardiology, Gastroenterology, Dermatology, Endocrinology and Orthopedic Surgery (112,318 lines). Restricting the PCP definition to Family Medicine and Internal Medicine; the unrestricted version is reported as a discarded specification

Non-visit services excluded: POS 81 independent-lab lines (299,399), Radiology professional lines at POS 11 (49,836), and ED-side ancillaries (revenue 0250/0300/0320/0350/0636/0730) are not counted as visits

Right-censoring of the follow-up window: the last ED visit is 31 Dec 2025 and claims run through 14 Jan 2026, giving exactly 14 days of look-forward for every ED visit in the denominator. PCP visit supply is flat across 1-14 Jan 2026 (868/day vs 879/day in December), and December follow-up rates by week of ED visit show no decline, so no attenuation at the end of the panel. (The 30-day sensitivity spec IS censored and is flagged as such)

Parallel pre-trends - the main threat, examined in detail. The pooled pre-period differential linear trend on the primary outcome is +0.97 pp/month (se 0.38, p = 0.014), and a placebo DiD inside the pre-period returns +2.93 pp, so the assumption is not cleanly satisfied. Decomposing: the clinic (G0463) channel, which carries +6.31 of the +8.06 pp, has a flat differential pre-trend (+0.11 pp/month, p = 0.55) and a razor-sharp June-to-July break of +8.17 pp against a maximum of +2.03 pp for any other month-to-month move in the year. The drift is confined to the office channel (+0.65 pp/month, p = 0.098) and is driven by control-arm sampling noise (control office rate wanders 26.8-30.5 pp across the six pre-months on ~1,300 ED visits/month, SE about 1.3 pp), not by a treated-arm trend: the treated office rate is flat pre-period (23.0-24.6) and then jumps with zero overlap (26.5-28.4 post). Net judgement: the sign and significance are robust, the magnitude is sensitive. Trend-robust variants span +5.65 to +8.96 pp (June-baseline +6.05, group-specific trends +7.21 to +8.96, channel-wise trend adjustment +5.65 for the clinic channel); only the aggressive 6-month linear extrapolation of a 6-point noisy pre-trend pulls the point estimate to +2.29 pp, and that adjustment removes the office component while leaving the clinic component intact
Treatment timing: all 30 program practices share launch_date 2025-07-01, so there is no staggered adoption and no negative-weighting problem; a simple 2x2 DiD is the right estimator

Denominator selection (did the program change who shows up in the ED?): ED visits per attributed member were 0.1289 pre and 0.1303 post for program practices vs 0.1308 and 0.1329 for comparison practices; DiD on ED visits per member -0.0007, p = 0.80. Group sizes are balanced (1,991 vs 1,994 members per practice; 30 practices each)
ED case-mix shift: acuity distribution (99281-99285) is stable; DiD on the share of high-acuity (99284/99285) ED visits is -0.0008, p = 0.94. Adding acuity controls leaves the estimate at +8.06 pp

Attribution stability: zero members change practice_id over the panel, and no claim spans multiple members, dates, practices, claim types or places of service, so there is no attribution churn or claim-splitting to handle

Is the program creating visits or just relabelling/retiming them? Post-ED clinic visits per member rose by +0.0078 (p < 0.001) in program practices while non-post-ED clinic visits were unchanged (+0.0012, p = 0.80) and total clinic volume rose +0.0090 (p = 0.057) - the follow-ups are mostly net-new encounters. The marginal post-ED clinic visits look like ordinary visits, not navigation overhead: 96% revenue 0517 (family practice clinic), mean allowed $112 (vs $115 for all others), 79% with same-day labs, and none fall on the ED date itself. Non-post-ED office visits fell slightly in program practices (-0.0174, p = 0.048), so total primary care volume was flat (DiD -0.0057, p = 0.58)

Effect breadth, not a few outlier practices: all 30 program practices increased their follow-up rate (mean +8.74 pp, sd 3.66) versus 17 of 30 comparison practices (mean +0.74 pp, sd 4.04); Wilcoxon rank-sum p = 1.0e-08

Inference with few clusters: 60 practices, so CR1 SEs are paired with t(59) critical values and cross-checked against a wild cluster bootstrap, member-level clustering, HC1, a practice-period collapsed regression, a practice-level t-test and randomization inference - all give essentially the same interval
Functional form: a logit on the same four terms implies the identical +8.06 pp discrete DiD, so the linear probability model is not distorting anything at these rates (30-39%)

Window definition: same-day follow-up (11-12% of all follow-ups) is included per the stated definition; excluding it gives +7.71 pp, a 7-day window +2.42 pp, so the result is not an artifact of the window edge
headline_claim: The care-navigation program raised the 14-day ED-to-PCP follow-up rate by about 8 percentage points (95% CI 6.0 to 10.1), from 29.7% to 38.5% at program practices while comparison practices were flat at 35.8% to 36.6% - a real and broad-based improvement (all 30 program practices improved), though the precise magnitude is sensitive to pre-trend assumptions and a defensible range is roughly 6 to 9 points.
